name: Genoa strikes the genovino d'oro
summary: In 1252 the Genoese and Florentine mints simultaneously began striking high-value gold coins, the genovino d'oro at Genoa and the fiorino at Florence, the first stable gold coinages in the Latin West for more than five centuries. The 3.5-gram coin was rapidly imitated by Venice's ducato (1284) and used as the high-denomination unit for trans-Mediterranean and Levantine trade.

_quarry.structural_significance: Marks the point at which Latin-European mints had access to enough African and Asian gold via Mediterranean trade routes to support a bimetallic currency. Lopez treats the simultaneous Genoa/Florence strikings as a structural symptom of the thirteenth-century commercial revolution.
